To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) CXCR4 and its ligand SDF-1 are key players in the regulation of organogenesis, stem/progenitor cell mobilization, tissue regeneration and tumorigenicity, 2) CXCR4+ stem/progenitor cells are deposited early during development, 3) CXCR4 expression is upregulated in the damaged tissue and in cancer, 4) CXCR4 antagonists may lead to new therapies in regenerative medicine and oncology.
the SDF- 1– CXCR4 axis plays a pivotal role not only in organogenesis but also in regeneration of damaged tissues and in tumorigenesis.
the SDF- 1-CXCR4 axis is a key regulator of organogenesis, regeneration, and tumorigenensis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the pleiotropic effects that the SDF- 1–CXCR axis has in organ development, regeneration and cancer.
the pleiotropic effects exerted by the CXCR4–SDF-1 axis during organogenesis, tissue regeneration and cancer.
the role of SDF-1 and CXCR4 in the regulation of NSC and CSC motogenesis and homing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SDF- 1–CXCR 4 axis is involved in the development and renewal/regrowth of tissues, and that this axis is also involved in cancer metastasis.
the SDF- 1–CXCR axis is a key player in the regulation of NSC homing and migration during organogenesis and tissue renewal/regeneration.
SDF-1 and CXCR4 are important regulators of stem cell biology in both development and tumorigenics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

SDF-1/CXCR4 is a key regulator in organogenesis and regeneration, and that the SDF- 1– CXCR4 axis plays a pivotal role as an organizer of the tissue microenvironment and as a key player in the regulation of the stem/progenitor cell niche.
the SDF- 1–CXCR1/2/3/CXCR4 axis plays an important role in organogenesis, tissue renewal/regeneration, and cancer progression and metastasis.
CXCR4 and its ligand SDF-1 are important regulators of NSC and CSC motility and homing to damaged tissue/organs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SDF-1/CXCR4 axis plays a pivotal role not only in organogenesis, but also in regeneration, tissue repair, and cancer metastasis.
the SDF- 1–CXCR axis may be a promising target for therapeutic intervention.

the pleiotropic effects in organogenesis, renewal/regeneration and tumorigeness of the SDF1–CXCR axis are the result of the ability of CXCR4 to sense the concentration of SDF1 and respond accordingly.
